name: SUECA
description: Sueca (Portuguese: 'Swedish') is the most popular card game in Portugal and Brazil. It is a trick-taking game for 4 players in two partnerships. The game uses a 40-card deck and is notable for its Ace-Seven-King-Jack-Queen hierarchy (similar to Briscola or Tressette, but with 7 as 10 points). The goal is to take more than half the points (61+) in tricks. No talking is allowed.

content.text: Sueca (Portuguese: 'Swedish') is the most popular card game in Portugal and Brazil. It is a trick-taking game for 4 players in two partnerships. The game uses a 40-card deck and is notable for its Ace-Seven-King-Jack-Queen hierarchy (similar to Briscola or Tressette, but with 7 as 10 points). The goal is to take more than half the points (61+) in tricks. No talking is allowed.
Likely derives from Tressette or similar Italian games, perhaps brought by Swedish sailors?
Standard 52-card deck with the 8s, 9s and 10s removed, leaving 40 cards. Four suits; rank in each suit from high to low: Ace, 7 (manilha), King, Jack, Queen, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2.
Deal 10 cards to each player. Bottom card turned for Trump.

items.text: Brazil (clockwise): In Brazil play is clockwise; dealing and lead order follow local convention.
Revoke penalty: Some play that revoke (failing to follow suit when able) costs the offending team two games.
Azores (10 as manilha): In the Azores the 10 is often the manilha (second highest). Trump determined by cutting the packet of 12 rejected cards (9s, 8s, 7s) instead of turning a card.
